# Godot 4 UI With Focus Navigation

## Background

Build a nested Godot 4 UI menu that works with both mouse and keyboard/gamepad focus navigation. The project must run under headless Godot for automated verification.

## Requirements

* Implement a `MainMenu` and a `SettingsMenu` scene, and a `RootUI` scene that owns and toggles them via `visible` (no scene swap).
* Wire up an `ui_back` input action mapped to both `escape` and a joypad button so the settings menu can be dismissed.
* Provide a `GameSettings` autoload that stores volume, resolution index, and fullscreen state, and exposes a `settings_changed` signal.
* Wire focus neighbors so the main menu buttons cycle vertically and the settings controls form a working focus chain.

## Implementation Hints

* Use Godot 4 `Control` nodes; configure `focus_neighbor_top` / `focus_neighbor_bottom` and `focus_neighbor_left` / `focus_neighbor_right` to chain controls explicitly.
* Edit `project.godot` so the input map and autoload entries exist before running headless.
* Use signals such as `value_changed`, `item_selected`, and `toggled` to push values into the `GameSettings` autoload, and emit `settings_changed` from the autoload.
* Use `Input.action_press("ui_back")` style APIs from a verifier script; the SettingsMenu should listen for that action and hide itself while re-showing the MainMenu.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Project path: /home/user/myproject
* Command: godot --headless --path /home/user/myproject --script res\://verify.gd
* The Godot project at the project path must satisfy all of the following:
  * `project.godot` defines an `input/ui_back` action whose `events` list contains an `InputEventKey` for the Escape key AND an `InputEventJoypadButton` (button index 1).
  * `project.godot` registers `GameSettings` as an autoload pointing at the script `res://autoloads/GameSettings.gd`.
  * Scene `res://scenes/MainMenu.tscn` exists and contains a `VBoxContainer` with three `Button` children whose text is `Play`, `Settings`, and `Quit` (in order). The buttons' `focus_neighbor_top` and `focus_neighbor_bottom` form a vertical wrap-around cycle Play -> Settings -> Quit -> Play.
  * Scene `res://scenes/SettingsMenu.tscn` exists and contains, anywhere in its tree, an `HSlider`, an `OptionButton` with exactly 3 items, a `CheckBox`, and a `Button` whose text is `Back`.
  * Scene `res://scenes/RootUI.tscn` exists, instances both menus, and shows `MainMenu` while hiding `SettingsMenu` on `_ready`.
  * When the verifier runs `RootUI`, makes `SettingsMenu` visible, then calls `Input.action_press("ui_back")` and pumps a frame, the `SettingsMenu` becomes invisible and `MainMenu` becomes visible.
  * Setting the `HSlider.value` to `0.42` causes `GameSettings.volume` to equal `0.42` and emits the `settings_changed` signal on the `GameSettings` autoload at least once.
  * The autoload `GameSettings` is read in the SettingsMenu `_ready` so existing values are reflected in the controls.
* The script `res://verify.gd` is provided by the verifier (do not commit your own copy under that exact path); your project must work with it.

	main_menu.name = "MainMenu"
	main_menu.set_script(load("res://scenes/MainMenu.gd"))
	
	var vbox = VBoxContainer.new()
	vbox.name = "VBoxContainer"
	main_menu.add_child(vbox)
	vbox.owner = main_menu
	
	var btn_play = Button.new()
	btn_play.name = "Play"
	btn_play.text = "Play"
	vbox.add_child(btn_play)
	btn_play.owner = main_menu
	
	var btn_settings = Button.new()
	btn_settings.name = "Settings"
	btn_settings.text = "Settings"
	vbox.add_child(btn_settings)
	btn_settings.owner = main_menu
	
	var btn_quit = Button.new()
	btn_quit.name = "Quit"
	btn_quit.text = "Quit"
	vbox.add_child(btn_quit)
	btn_quit.owner = main_menu
	
	btn_play.focus_neighbor_bottom = NodePath("../Settings")
	btn_play.focus_neighbor_top = NodePath("../Quit")
	
	btn_settings.focus_neighbor_bottom = NodePath("../Quit")
	btn_settings.focus_neighbor_top = NodePath("../Play")
	
	btn_quit.focus_neighbor_bottom = NodePath("../Play")
	btn_quit.focus_neighbor_top = NodePath("../Settings")
	
	var pack_main = PackedScene.new()
	pack_main.pack(main_menu)
	ResourceSaver.save(pack_main, "res://scenes/MainMenu.tscn")
	
	# 2. Create SettingsMenu.tscn
	var settings_menu = Control.new()
	settings_menu.name = "SettingsMenu"
	settings_menu.set_script(load("res://scenes/SettingsMenu.gd"))
	
	var vbox_s = VBoxContainer.new()
	vbox_s.name = "VBoxContainer"
	settings_menu.add_child(vbox_s)
	vbox_s.owner = settings_menu
	
	var slider = HSlider.new()
	slider.name = "VolumeSlider"
	slider.min_value = 0.0
	slider.max_value = 1.0
	slider.step = 0.01
	vbox_s.add_child(slider)
	slider.owner = settings_menu
	
	var opt_res = OptionButton.new()
	opt_res.name = "ResolutionOption"
	vbox_s.add_child(opt_res)
	opt_res.owner = settings_menu
	
	var chk_full = CheckBox.new()
	chk_full.name = "FullscreenCheck"
	vbox_s.add_child(chk_full)
	chk_full.owner = settings_menu
	
	var btn_back = Button.new()
	btn_back.name = "BackButton"
	btn_back.text = "Back"
	vbox_s.add_child(btn_back)
	btn_back.owner = settings_menu
	
	slider.focus_neighbor_bottom = NodePath("../ResolutionOption")
	slider.focus_neighbor_top = NodePath("../BackButton")
	
	opt_res.focus_neighbor_bottom = NodePath("../FullscreenCheck")
	opt_res.focus_neighbor_top = NodePath("../VolumeSlider")
	
	chk_full.focus_neighbor_bottom = NodePath("../BackButton")
	chk_full.focus_neighbor_top = NodePath("../ResolutionOption")
	
	btn_back.focus_neighbor_bottom = NodePath("../VolumeSlider")
	btn_back.focus_neighbor_top = NodePath("../FullscreenCheck")
	
	var pack_settings = PackedScene.new()
	pack_settings.pack(settings_menu)
	ResourceSaver.save(pack_settings, "res://scenes/SettingsMenu.tscn")
	
	# 3. Create RootUI.tscn
	var root_ui = Control.new()
	root_ui.name = "RootUI"
	root_ui.set_script(load("res://scenes/RootUI.gd"))
	
	var inst_main = load("res://scenes/MainMenu.tscn").instantiate()
	root_ui.add_child(inst_main)
	inst_main.owner = root_ui
	
	var inst_settings = load("res://scenes/SettingsMenu.tscn").instantiate()
	root_ui.add_child(inst_settings)
	inst_settings.owner = root_ui
	
	var pack_root = PackedScene.new()
	pack_root.pack(root_ui)
	ResourceSaver.save(pack_root, "res://scenes/RootUI.tscn")
	
	print("Scenes generated successfully!")
	quit()

		return

	get_root().remove_child(settings_menu)
	settings_menu.queue_free()

	# 5. Check RootUI scene
	var root_ui_scene = load("res://scenes/RootUI.tscn")
	if not root_ui_scene:
		print("FAIL: RootUI.tscn not found")
		quit(1)
		return
	var root_ui = root_ui_scene.instantiate()
	get_root().add_child(root_ui)

		quit(1)
		return

	print("Transitioned to SettingsMenu:")
	print("  MainMenu visible: ", r_main.visible)
	print("  SettingsMenu visible: ", r_settings.visible)

I'm currently examining the `SettingsMenu.gd` file, specifically focusing on the `_ready` function and how it interacts with `game_settings`. I'm also reviewing the `_on_volume_changed` signal handler.

input.searchContent:
func _ready():
	print("SettingsMenu _ready starting. game_settings is: ", game_settings)
	# Load existing settings from GameSettings autoload
	volume_slider.value = game_settings.volume
	
	# OptionButton needs exactly 3 items
	resolution_option.clear()
	resolution_option.add_item("1280x720")
	resolution_option.add_item("1920x1080")
	resolution_option.add_item("2560x1440")
	resolution_option.selected = game_settings.resolution_index
	
	fullscreen_check.button_pressed = game_settings.fullscreen
	
	# Connect signals to update GameSettings autoload
	volume_slider.value_changed.connect(_on_volume_changed)
	resolution_option.item_selected.connect(_on_resolution_selected)
	fullscreen_check.toggled.connect(_on_fullscreen_toggled)
	back_button.pressed.connect(_on_back_pressed)

func _process(_delta):
	if visible and Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_back"):
		_on_back_pressed()

func _on_volume_changed(val: float):
	print("SettingsMenu _on_volume_changed called with: ", val)
	game_settings.volume = val

I have successfully implemented the nested Godot 4 UI menu with robust focus navigation support and automated verification readiness under headless Godot.

Here is a summary of the implemented features:

1. **Project Settings (`project.godot`)**:
   - Defined the `input/ui_back` action, mapped to both the **Escape key** (`InputEventKey` with physical_keycode/keycode `4194305`) and a **joypad button** with index 1 (`InputEventJoypadButton`).
   - Registered `GameSettings` as an autoload pointing at `res://autoloads/GameSettings.gd`.

2. **`GameSettings` Autoload (`res://autoloads/GameSettings.gd`)**:
   - Stores `volume` (float), `resolution_index` (int), and `fullscreen` (bool).
   - Exposes the `settings_changed` signal, emitted whenever any of the property values are updated via their GDScript property setters.

3. **`MainMenu` Scene (`res://scenes/MainMenu.tscn` & `MainMenu.gd`)**:
   - Contains a `VBoxContainer` with three `Button` children: `Play`, `Settings`, and `Quit` (in order).
   - Explicitly configured vertical focus wrap-around (`focus_neighbor_top` and `focus_neighbor_bottom`) forming a cycle: Play ↔ Settings ↔ Quit ↔ Play.

4. **`SettingsMenu` Scene (`res://scenes/SettingsMenu.tscn` & `SettingsMenu.gd`)**:
   - Contains an `HSlider` (`VolumeSlider`), an `OptionButton` (`ResolutionOption`) with exactly 3 resolution items, a `CheckBox` (`FullscreenCheck`), and a `Button` with the text `"Back"` (`BackButton`).
   - Formed a robust, explicit vertical focus chain between all controls to support keyboard/gamepad focus navigation.
   - Reads existing values from the `GameSettings` autoload in `_ready` to reflect them on the controls.
   - Updates `GameSettings` values and triggers the `settings_changed` signal when controls are changed (such as setting the slider value to `0.42`).

5. **`RootUI` Scene (`res://scenes/RootUI.tscn` & `RootUI.gd`)**:
   - Instances both `MainMenu` and `SettingsMenu`, displaying `MainMenu` while hiding `SettingsMenu` on `_ready`.
   - Listens for the `ui_back` input action. When `ui_back` is pressed while `SettingsMenu` is visible, it hides `SettingsMenu` and restores visibility to `MainMenu` (and grabs focus back on the Settings button).

The project is fully verified to be completely operational and compliant with the acceptance criteria!
